body:
Anika (infra): Heads-up — we need to decide final admission-control behavior for regional GPU saturation. Reject vs degrade vs queue. Deadline EOD Friday.
Marco (sre): +1 we saw the eu-west spike yesterday. queue lengths shot up, then lots of client retries.
Priya (eng-runtime): Observed two failure modes: 1) immediate rejects => client retries amplify load, 2) long queues => p99 latency breaks SLAs. Both bad.
Evan (product): From product side, we prefer graceful degradation over hard rejects if UX can be explained (e.g., smaller model). But latency >5s is also bad for our use cases.
sre-bot: incident: region eu-west reached 96% GPU util at 2026-02-15T11:08Z, queued_requests=420, rejects=12.
Anika (infra): Thinking hybrid policy: short soft-queue (e.g., 2s), then degrade to smaller/quantized model, then reject as last resort. Thoughts?
Marco (sre): I'm worried about memory/kv-cache mismatch when we switch model mid-request. That can blow tail memory. Need a clear fast-path for degrade that uses compatible kv/cache layout.
Priya (eng-runtime): Agreed. We can implement degrade only to compatible-family variants (same architecture, lower params/quantized). No cross-arch fallback. That keeps KV semantics intact.
Priya (eng-runtime): Proposed policy (pseudo-config):
```
admission:
  soft_queue_ms: 2000
  degrade_to_model_tags: ["opt-6q", "opt-4n"]
  max_queue_per_gpu: 8
  reject_if_queue_gt: 50
```
Evan (product): Can we expose a header so clients can know they got a degraded model? e.g., `x-redwood-model-fallback` so UI can surface a message.
Anika (infra): yes, include header + metric (counter per-tenant). Must be opt-in for enterprise customers? some contracts require non-degraded.
Marco (sre): Also enforce per-tenant SLA exemptions: if tenant has `no_degrade` flag, we should bypass degrade and either queue longer (if allowed) or reject based on config.
Priya (eng-runtime): That implies admission decision needs tenant metadata lookup in hot-path. We can cache flags in local node for 30s. Cost: extra mem and cache-coherency but doable.
Anika (infra): What about queue policy: FIFO with priority bump for real-time routes? Or token-bucket per-route?
Marco (sre): Suggest priority tiers: realtime (short fifo, max 4 per-gpu), interactive (soft-queue 2s), batch (longer queue, preemptible). Also preemptible batch can be evicted when headroom needed.
Priya (eng-runtime): Preemption adds complexity; need to track KV cache warm-up cost. Evicting a batch frees compute but loses cached context. We should prefer not to preempt active interactive requests.
sre-bot: telemetry note: implement metrics: admission_soft_queued, admission_degraded_count, admission_rejected_count, average_queue_ms, per-region_gpu_headroom.
Evan (product): Rollout plan? Small canary in one region then ramp. Product wants 1%->10%->50%->100% with kill switch.
Anika (infra): Ops plan: canary in us-west1 with degraded-model pool pre-warmed, 1% traffic for 24h. Monitor: p99 latency, degrade_rate, retry_rate, errors. Kill if p99 > 3x baseline or retry_rate spikes > 2x.
Priya (eng-runtime): We'll add a feature flag `admission.hybrid_v1` and a toggle per-region. Implementation ETA 3 days, canary config ETA 1 day after.
Marco (sre): Cost note: degrading to smaller models reduces GPU token cost but may increase requests due to additional generation if outputs worse. Need to measure quality -> downstream conversion delta. Put cost-quality metric in dashboard.
Evan (product): We'll prepare a small experiment with two routes: A=degrade fallback, B=reject with client retry backoff, then compare user-facing metrics.
Anika (infra): Action items: Priya implement hybrid policy + headers (owner Priya), Marco add dashboards and alert thresholds (owner Marco), Evan design UX and experiment (owner Evan). Can we commit to EOD Friday for the proposal and Monday for canary rollout?
Priya (eng-runtime): I'll open PR today with config and a unit test for kv-compatibility path.
Marco (sre): I'll add alert playbook and dashboards.
Evan (product): I'll write experiment spec and notify growth.
Anika (infra): Great. Final note: keep reject as last resort — but for tenants with `no_degrade` we may need to reject earlier to protect overall headroom. Document that clearly in the rollout. :thumbsup:
sre-bot: deploy-bot: feature flag `admission.hybrid_v1` created for region us-west1.
Anika (infra): Thanks — will sync Friday 09:30 to finalize.
